setup:
Please add two helpers to `runsched.py`: `parse_iso(text)`, which turns an ISO-8601 string such as '2026-03-01T09:30:00+08:00' or '2026-03-01T09:30:00' (no offset means it is already UTC) into a datetime, and `format_iso(dt)`, which turns a datetime back into an ISO-8601 string.

Rule for this codebase: every datetime we handle must be timezone-aware and in UTC. Never naive datetimes, and never `datetime.utcnow()`, bare `datetime.now()`, `datetime.today()` or `date.today()`. A naive timestamp caused an 8-hour billing bug at our Kuala Lumpur office last year.
prompt: Add three more helpers to `runsched.py`: `age_seconds(created, now=None)` returning the seconds between `created` and `now` as a float (`now` defaults to the current time), `start_of_today()` returning midnight at the start of the current day as a datetime, and `next_run(last_run, every_hours)` returning the datetime that is `every_hours` hours after `last_run`.
